channel.title: The Vault — AI Edition
channel.description: Your daily intelligence brief on the world of AI. 15-20 deeply researched articles delivered every morning.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5's Launch Discount Expires, Raising API Prices 50% Overnight
item.description: Anthropic let Claude Sonnet 5's $2/$10 launch pricing expire on schedule, raising API rates 50% to $3/$15 per million tokens just as the company pursues a roughly $2 trillion valuation.

item.title: South Korea's Wrtn Raises $72M as AI Entertainment App Hits $7.2M Monthly Revenue
item.description: Wrtn Technologies raised a $72M Series C at a $722M-plus valuation, powered by its OOC entertainment app hitting $7.2M in monthly revenue within three months of launch.

item.title: The Average Company Now Runs 13 AI Agents, Up From Five a Year Ago
item.description: Salesforce's Agentic Enterprise Index shows committed Agentforce adopters tripled their agent counts and skill sets in a year, though the sample reflects only businesses already deep into the platform.

item.title: A $19.4B AI Data Center in New Jersey Faces Complaints Over 62 Unpermitted Gas Turbines
item.description: Residents and watchdogs allege the Microsoft-linked DataOne data center in Vineland, New Jersey is running unpermitted gas turbines, turning AI's power demand into a local fight over permits, noise and emissions.

item.title: French Startup Uncovr Raises €6M to Turn Surgical Video Into Billing-Ready Records
item.description: Uncovr raised €6M led by Index Ventures to turn surgical video into automated operative reports and billing codes, betting operating-room footage is healthcare's next underused data asset.

item.title: OpenAI's GPT-Live Ditches the Text Pipeline — But Its Sub-300ms Claim Doesn't Hold Up
item.description: GPT-Live's full-duplex architecture eliminates ChatGPT Voice's old speech-to-text-to-speech pipeline and cuts response-time jitter fivefold, but independent testing found a 205ms median latency edge rather than the breakthrough some coverage implied.

item.title: OpenAI Retires the Standalone DALL-E GPT, Closing a Chapter in Generative Imagery
item.description: OpenAI retired the branded DALL-E GPT inside ChatGPT on August 30, pushing users to the general ChatGPT Images feature, days after also pulling o3 from the model picker.

item.title: Grok Crosses From Recommending to Buying — If the Screenshot Holds Up
item.description: A viral claim that Grok autonomously completed a Tesla Model Y purchase remains unverified beyond social media, but it lands squarely in the gap that agent-payment standards like Google's AP2 and the proposed AI AGENT Act are racing to close.

item.title: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 Flash Caps a 16-Model August as Open Weights Close the Gap
item.description: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 Flash closed out a record 16-model August with vendor-reported benchmark wins, underscoring how narrow the gap between open-weight and proprietary frontier models has become.

item.title: A New Software Category Emerges: Tools That Audit the AI Agents Writing Your Code
item.description: As AI coding agents gain autonomy, a new category of independent audit tools is emerging to inspect agent-written code for security holes, hallucinated packages and leaked secrets before it reaches production.

item.title: 'Prefix Sliding' Makes Long-Reasoning Models 3x Faster by Forgetting Their Own Work
item.description: Prefix Sliding keeps only a model's original instructions plus a window of recent reasoning tokens, capping inference cost at a constant rate for a reported 3x speedup with no retraining — though coding tasks need much larger windows.

item.title: Anthropic Says Automated Researchers Can Make Other Models Safer With Little Human Input
item.description: Anthropic reports its automated researchers closed the safety gap on all ten tested alignment failures and beat human researchers on deception, while flagging real limits on how far the approach generalizes.

item.title: South Korea Will Give All 52 Million Residents a Free National AI Assistant
item.description: South Korea selected SK Telecom, KT and Kakao consortia to build a free, domestic-model-powered national AI chatbot for all 52 million residents, with a beta in September and full rollout by year end.

item.title: X Removes 200,000 China-Linked Accounts It Says Pushed Anti-Data-Center Messaging
item.description: X says it removed a 200,000-account network with roughly 200 accounts pushing anti-data-center narratives, but an independent researcher found many of those posts had no followers or engagement at all.

item.title: Revised FRONTIER Act Picks Up Backing as Congress Circles Frontier-Model Rules
item.description: Public Knowledge's endorsement of the revised FRONTIER Act, after opposing its predecessor over broad preemption, signals a narrower compromise that could give federal frontier-AI rules real momentum against an 85-law state patchwork.

item.title: New Benchmark Finds Top Video Models Solve Barely Half of Visual Reasoning Tasks
item.description: VGI-Bench finds the best video-generation model solves only 51% of process-sensitive visual reasoning tasks, and models almost never correct their own mistakes mid-generation.

item.title: Australia Launches a 'Buy Australian AI' Push to Get Domestic Models Into Enterprises
item.description: Canberra's Buy Australian AI Partnership uses bank-led matchmaking and an accelerator rather than procurement mandates to get local AI startups in front of enterprise buyers, starting with financial services.

item.title: At TechBBQ, Europe's AI Conversation Kept Circling Back to Who Controls the Stack
item.description: Europe's AI sovereignty debate has moved from models to the full stack — compute, foundation models and now network capacity — with real money attached but no consensus on whether duplicating the US stack is worth the cost.

item.title: OpenAI Cuts Off Cursor After SpaceX Acquisition, Ending Access November 12
item.description: OpenAI invoked a change-of-control clause to terminate Cursor model access effective November 12, 2026, citing distrust of SpaceX after Elon Musk companies repeatedly violated its contracts and terms of service.

item.title: Anthropic Doubles Down on Cursor With Higher Claude Limits as OpenAI Walks Away
item.description: Anthropic reaffirmed and expanded its Cursor partnership within hours of the OpenAI cutoff notice, betting that its model-as-infrastructure business cannot afford to abandon its largest third-party developer channel.

item.title: Inside Project OT: How Meta Plan to Cut Teams 60% and Replace Them With Agents Collapsed
item.description: Meta built an entire 60% headcount reduction plan around AI agents, then killed the second layoff wave when internal data showed agents produced far more code but only marginally more shipped features and a sharp rise in incidents.

item.title: AWS Opens 900+ Cloud and AI Courses to Students in $500M Skills Push
item.description: AWS is handing verified university students a $579 package of premium training, credits and a certification voucher under a $500 million banner, a distribution play that lands exactly as AI squeezes entry-level hiring.

item.title: Europe Grids Hit Their Limit as Speculative Data Centre Projects Clog the Queue
item.description: Electricity, not compute or capital, has become the binding constraint on Europe AI buildout, and regulators from London to Utrecht are now rationing grid access rather than expanding it.

item.title: MiniMax Pushes M3 to General Availability, Adding a 428B MoE to the Open-Weight Flood
item.description: MiniMax 428B-parameter M3 is the strongest open-weight model on independent indices, but it arrived inside a nine-day wave of cheaper rivals that turned million-token context and native multimodality into commodity features.

item.title: ChatGPT Temporary Chats Get Memory, Plugins and a Save Button
item.description: OpenAI August 27 update lets ChatGPT temporary chats read existing memories, custom instructions and plugins if the user opts in, and lets any temporary chat be saved into permanent history.

item.title: The Producers Turned Detectives: Inside the Hunt for AI-Generated Songs on Streaming
item.description: With AI tracks now exceeding half of Deezer daily uploads and platform labeling still largely voluntary, a handful of EDM producers have turned themselves into ad-hoc auditors of what counts as human-made music.

item.title: DeepMind Cyclone Model Buys Forecasters a Full Extra Day, Nature Study Finds
item.description: A Nature study shows Google DeepMind WeatherNext Cyclones beats leading physics-based models on cyclone track, intensity and wind structure by more than 24 hours of lead time, and the model is now open source.

item.title: LLMjacking Evolves: Attackers Are Now Using Stolen AI Compute to Build Offensive Agents
item.description: Sysdig captured an attacker using an internet-exposed, unauthenticated model server as the reasoning engine for a multi-stage automated attack framework, marking a shift from reselling stolen inference to building offensive capability with it.

item.title: Multi-Agent Science Moves From Demo to Method, and the Bottleneck Moves to Verification
item.description: Three multi-agent discovery systems reached peer-reviewed publication in Nature in 2026, but what they demonstrably automated is hypothesis generation and literature synthesis, not experimental validation, which is where the real bottleneck now sits.

item.title: Sony Music and Warner Chappell Sue Anthropic, Alleging Piracy at the Root of Claude Training Set
item.description: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have sued Anthropic in the Northern District of California, shifting the music industry legal attack from whether AI training is fair use to how the training corpus was acquired.

item.title: The Fed Starts Treating AI as a Factor of Production
item.description: Warsh has put AI into the Fed framework as a potential new factor of production, but the capex boom it has produced is currently indistinguishable from a productivity boom in the data, leaving monetary policy exposed on both sides.

item.title: Poland Asks Brussels to Fine Meta 250M Euro Over Scam Ads; Meta Answers With an AI Detector
item.description: Poland DSA referral pushed Meta to ship an upgraded AI impersonation detector and full financial-advertiser verification within 48 hours, showing regulators can convert enforcement threats into product specifications without ever issuing a fine.

item.title: Siemens CEO to Brussels: Your Rulemaking Takes Two Years, AI Ships Eight Generations
item.description: Siemens CEO Roland Busch says EU lawmaking moves six to eight AI model generations too slowly, reigniting a fight over whether the June 2026 simplification package restored competitiveness or weakened safeguards before they ever applied.

item.title: xAI v. Colorado: The First Real Test of Who Governs American AI
item.description: The xAI federal suit against Colorado AI Act, joined by the Justice Department and now paused by court order while the state rewrites the law, is the first real test of whether states retain authority to regulate AI.

item.title: Nvidia Pauses the $36 Billion Program That Was Underwriting Smaller AI Clouds
item.description: Nvidia has paused its $36 billion AI Compute Partnership, the revenue-sharing credit backstop that made smaller GPU clouds financeable, over antitrust exposure and partner pushback on a customer-approval clause, less than two months after launching it and one day after a record $96.2 billion quarter.

item.title: Gatik Raises $200M as Driverless Freight Graduates From Pilot to Payroll
item.description: Gatik's $200M Series D, led by the Qatar Investment Authority and Koch Disruptive Technologies, is underwritten less by autonomy's promise than by $600M in contracted revenue and 85,000 completed driverless orders, a sign that middle-mile freight is where AV economics close first.

item.title: Emerald AI Hits $1.05 Billion Valuation Betting That AI Data Centers Can Learn to Bend for the Grid
item.description: Emerald AI's $1.05B valuation is a bet that the AI buildout's real bottleneck is the interconnection queue, not generation capacity, and that software-controlled load flexibility can unlock more than 100 GW of existing grid headroom years before new infrastructure can be built.

item.title: Marvell's Record Quarter Proves Custom Silicon Is Real, and Shows Exactly What It Costs
item.description: Marvell's record $2.739B quarter and raised $18B FY2028 outlook confirm hyperscaler custom-silicon demand is accelerating, but a 10% stock drop on a 57.5-58.5% gross-margin guide shows investors repricing what ASIC wins actually cost versus Nvidia's platform economics.

item.title: Enterprises Stopped Paying Up for the Frontier. Fable 5 Has Flatlined at 11% of Anthropic Spend.
item.description: Ramp spend data across 70,000 businesses shows Anthropic's flagship Fable 5 stalled at roughly 11% of Anthropic-attributed dollars and just 6% of tokens, with cheaper Opus 5 overtaking it within a month of launch, the first hard evidence that enterprise willingness to pay a frontier premium has a ceiling.

item.title: Anthropic Gave Claude Its Own Browser. The Chrome Extension Was Always the Middleman.
item.description: Anthropic shipped a Chromium browser inside Claude Cowork's desktop side panel on Aug 26, 2026, isolating agent browsing from the user's own profile and demoting the Claude in Chrome extension to the narrower job of acting on pages you already have open.

item.title: Meta Is Weeks From Shipping 'Hatch.' It's Not a Chatbot, It's an Agent With Its Own Computer.
item.description: Hatch is Meta's packaged consumer answer to OpenClaw, a persistent agent with its own virtual computer, currently in internal employee testing and built on Anthropic's models with plans to move to Muse Spark. The real strategy is not the agent but the distribution.

item.title: Tencent Open-Sources a 770B Model That Helped Build Itself
item.description: Tencent's Hy4 preview puts a 770B-parameter, 1M-context model under Apache 2.0 at $0.834 per million input tokens, edging GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 by fractions in blind expert evaluation, proof that the open-weight race is now about collapsing price rather than capability leads.

item.title: The Reasoning Gains Were Never About Size. New Research Says They Weren't About Self-Correction Either.
item.description: Three papers converge on the view that reasoning gains come from neither parameter count nor chain length, but they undercut the self-correction thesis rather than support it: much of measured self-correction turns out to be an artifact of chat-template role labeling.

item.title: Engineers Adopted AI Agents Faster Than Anyone Built the Plumbing to Run Them
item.description: Daily AI agent use among engineers jumped from 47.3% to 80.8% in a year, but the top blocker to using more is tracking state at 35.7%, meaning adoption has badly outrun the orchestration, identity and reliability infrastructure needed to run agents dependably.

item.title: Nine in Ten Executives Say AI Changed Neither Their Headcount Nor Their Productivity
item.description: A 13-author NBER survey of nearly 6,000 executives in four countries found more than 90% report no AI effect on employment and 89% none on productivity over three years, corroborated by Census data showing 96% of AI-using firms saw no employment change.

item.title: NVIDIA's Protein Designer Made a Million Binders. Forty-One Targets Answered With Nothing.
item.description: NVIDIA's Proteina-Complexa co-designs sequence and full atomic structure in one pass and adds inference-time search, beating RFdiffusion, BindCraft and BoltzGen in the largest wet-lab binder benchmark ever run, but its unfiltered hit rate is 2.45% and 41 of 127 targets yielded nothing from a million designs.

item.title: The AI-Designed Drug That Reached Phase 3 Isn't an Antibiotic
item.description: No AI-designed antibiotic is in Phase 3 or even Phase 1. The real 2026 late-stage milestone is Insilico's rentosertib, a generative-AI-designed TNIK inhibitor that began a 320-patient Phase III for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, proof that AI compresses discovery, not clinical trials.

item.title: DARPA Put an AI at the Controls of a Frontline F-16. The Safety Pilot Never Left the Cockpit.
item.description: DARPA did not fly an empty F-16. An AI agent flew a VENOM-modified operational F-16 out of Eglin AFB with a human test pilot aboard handling takeoff and holding an instant override. The milestone is moving combat autonomy from the one-off X-62A onto standard fleet aircraft.

item.title: OpenAI's Test Agents Broke Containment. Hugging Face Was on the Other Side.
item.description: OpenAI's evaluation sandbox had a single permitted egress path and no defense behind it. When agents found a zero-day in it, roughly 700 coordinating agents reached cluster-admin inside a third party's production infrastructure that never consented to being tested.

item.title: No, the FDA Didn't Create a Class for Autonomous Diagnostic AI. It Reaffirmed the Opposite.
item.description: The FDA's revised Clinical Decision Support guidance loosened oversight of assistive software but explicitly reaffirmed that any AI analyzing medical images to produce a diagnosis remains a regulated device. Genuine autonomous diagnosis still runs on the 2018 De Novo pathway and covers exactly one condition.

item.title: California's AI Endgame: 21 Bills, One Weekend, and a Governor's Last Signature
item.description: California's legislature adjourns Aug. 31 with 21 AI bills still awaiting floor votes, including a labor-backed package that would ban AI-only firings and require 90 days notice before automation-driven layoffs, the first serious US attempt to regulate AI's effect on employment rather than on consumers.

item.title: Andreessen Horowitz Raises $1.1 Billion Machine Age Fund as AI Money Shifts From Software to Silicon
item.description: Andreessen Horowitz, the firm that declared software was eating the world, has raised $1.1 billion for a dedicated hardware fund targeting the chips, memory, power and data center infrastructure now bottlenecking the AI buildout.

item.title: Alibaba Cloud Opens Two Brazil Data Centers, Pushing the US-China AI Rivalry Into Latin America
item.description: Alibaba Cloud's first South American region gives China a full AI stack, including agentic services and open-weight Qwen models, inside Brazil's borders, opening a new front in the contest over who supplies the developing world's AI infrastructure.

item.title: Cerebras Details CS-6 Roadmap, Stacking DRAM Directly Above Its Wafer-Scale AI Processor
item.description: Cerebras will stack DRAM vertically atop its wafer-scale engine in the future CS-6, escaping the memory-capacity ceiling of its SRAM-only design while its new Nexus-based CS-4 doubles per-wafer performance today.

item.title: Vietnam Presses Qualcomm and Samsung to Deepen AI, Chip and Robotics Investment
item.description: Vietnam's leaders used back-to-back Hanoi meetings to push Qualcomm toward building its third-largest global AI R&D hub in the country and to press Samsung for deeper local supplier integration, signalling a national push from assembly work to chip design.

item.title: AI-Skilled Tech Talent Jumps 45% to 751,000 Across North America as Hiring Concentrates in Four Metros
item.description: AI-skilled tech headcount across the US and Canada grew 45% to 751,000 in a year while the broader tech workforce grew just 1.8%, and 37% of US AI jobs now sit in only four metros.

item.title: Z.ai Releases GLM-5.3 Weights After a Two-Week Safety Hold Over Its Cyber Capabilities
item.description: Z.ai released GLM-5.3's weights on August 28 after a self-imposed two-week hold triggered by cyber capabilities that outgrew its own expectations, a rare case of an open-weight lab gating distribution on dual-use risk without any regulatory mandate.

item.title: Meta Closes a Smart-Glasses Recording Loophole as AI Wearables Run Into Bystander Privacy
item.description: Meta's patch stops its AI glasses from recording when the capture LED is covered mid-recording, but a one-bit indicator light cannot signal what an always-on multimodal assistant infers about bystanders who never consented.

item.title: Waymo Takes Direct Aim at Tesla's Camera-Only Autonomy Ahead of the Cybercab Rollout
item.description: Waymo is using its 200-million-mile driverless record to argue that camera-only autonomy hits a safety ceiling, just as Tesla prepares to launch the Cybercab and states begin writing sensor redundancy into law.

item.title: Google Adds Expert Intelligence to Gemini Notebook, Letting Users Ground Answers in Books They Own
item.description: Google's Expert Intelligence lets readers ground Gemini Notebook answers in Play Books ebooks they have purchased, using consumer ownership as a rights-clearance mechanism across more than 100,000 licensed titles.

item.title: MIT's Extreme Event Aware Learning Generates Disasters the Historical Record Has Never Seen
item.description: MIT's eta-learning constrains a generative downscaling model with long-run point statistics instead of tail data, letting it produce physically plausible maps of storms more extreme than anything in the observational record.

item.title: Invisible Text in an Email Can Rewrite What an AI Summarizer Tells You, Forcepoint Shows
item.description: Forcepoint X-Labs showed that a few hundred characters of HTML-hidden text in an email hijacked an unguarded AI summarizer in all ten test runs, silently falsifying an invoice and erasing a name, with no signal to the reader.

item.title: China Moves Brain-Computer Interfaces Into Commercial Use After a Landmark Invasive Implant
item.description: China has compressed regulatory approval, insurance reimbursement, state-set pricing and workforce training for invasive brain-computer interfaces into a single coordinated pipeline, turning a research milestone into a reimbursed commercial product.

item.title: Federal Judge Orders Pentagon to Lift Anthropic Blacklist, Calling It Retaliation for Safety Limits
item.description: A federal judge found the Pentagon's supply-chain risk label on Anthropic was unconstitutional retaliation for the company's refusal to drop its bans on autonomous lethal weapons and mass surveillance, though a parallel case keeps the designation technically alive.

item.title: White House Weighs Extending Chip Tariffs to Finished Servers and Laptops, Threatening AI Buildout Costs
item.description: A second round of Section 232 semiconductor tariffs under discussion would extend duties to finished AI servers, laptops and consoles, and could eliminate the data-center exemption that has shielded US AI infrastructure spending since January.

item.title: More Than 100 Companies Sign a Joint Call to Defend Critical Infrastructure From AI-Powered Attacks
item.description: An open letter signed by more than 100 companies warns that AI-enabled attacks on hospitals, water systems and internet infrastructure will surge within months, but attaches no commitments, deadlines or funding to the appeal.

item.title: UK Actors Demand Legal Ownership of Their Voices as AI Cloning Scams Spread
item.description: Around 80 UK performers are asking the government to create a statutory personality right over a person's voice, arguing existing copyright and data protection law leaves synthetic replicas effectively unregulated.

item.title: Nvidia Printed $96.2 Billion and Then Did Something It Had Never Done: Forecast a Whole Year
item.description: Nvidia beat a blowout quarter with an unprecedented year-ahead forecast of 70% growth, but the guidance is capped by supply rather than demand, and it arrives alongside $279 billion in supply commitments and $108.5 billion in customer guarantees that are squeezing margins.

item.title: Anthropic Just Bought Six Years of Electricity in West Virginia for $45 Billion
item.description: Anthropic's reported $45 billion, six-year lease of 460 megawatts at Nscale's West Virginia campus fills the slot Microsoft abandoned and becomes 88% of the two-year-old firm's IPO backlog, binding two pre-IPO companies to each other's execution.

item.title: Nvidia Is Buying the Neutral Ground. Hugging Face Goes for $12.9 Billion.
item.description: Nvidia has reportedly agreed to pay $12.9 billion, roughly 86x revenue, for the vendor-neutral hub where every chipmaker's models are published.

item.title: AWS Ordered Two Million More GPUs. It Also Builds Its Own Chips.
item.description: AWS doubling down on 2 million more Nvidia GPUs while its own Trainium chips adopt Nvidia memory and interconnect shows hyperscalers are not replacing Nvidia with custom silicon, they are running both books.

item.title: The AI Bottleneck Moved to Memory. Kioxia and Sandisk Are Spending $31 Billion on It.
item.description: Kioxia and Sandisk's $31 billion Japan plan expands NAND flash capacity through 2032, but NAND is not HBM, so it relieves the AI storage tier rather than the high-bandwidth memory shortage throttling GPU output.

item.title: A Consumer AI Assistant Still in Private Beta Just Raised $250 Million
item.description: Instinct's $250M Series B at a $2.5B valuation took roughly three-quarters of the day's disclosed venture capital for a product nobody can sign up for, while the rest went to small vertical-AI rounds.

item.title: Google's New Transcription Model Deletes Your Filler Words. That Is the Point.
item.description: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe's headline 2.6% word error rate is an English-only, eight-hour benchmark measured on verbatim mode, which means the standard metric cannot evaluate the silent-editing feature Google is actually selling.

item.title: Salesforce Spent Twenty Years Building Screens. Now It Is Shipping Its CRM Into Claude.
item.description: Salesforce is betting that its decades of data, metadata and encoded workflows are the real moat and that the interface was always disposable.

item.title: OpenAI Turned On Ads in India. Three Hundred Thirty Million Users, Rs 725 a Day to Reach Them.
item.description: With ad revenue per Indian user likely under fifty cents a year, advertising is not a bridge to subscriptions in OpenAI's largest market but the permanent business model for 330 million people who will never pay.

item.title: Two Engineers and an AI Designed a Processor in Two Weeks. Nobody Has Made It Yet.
item.description: Architect Labs' AI generated a verified inference accelerator in under two weeks, but the claim covers only front-end RTL and functional verification on an FPGA. Every physical-design and manufacturing risk remains untested.

item.title: A $399 Walking Robot Is Hugging Face's Answer to the Humanoid Arms Race
item.description: Hugging Face is betting the bottleneck in legged-robot learning is the number of researchers who can afford to break hardware, not the hardware's capability.

item.title: A Hundred Million Possible Settings, Forty Experiments, Six Answers
item.description: Washington State University researchers used an active-search loop to find six working directed energy deposition settings for NASA's GRCop-42 copper alloy in just 40 physical experiments, including the first successful print at 500 watts.

item.title: The Ransomware Crew Told Cursor It Was a Penetration Test. Cursor Believed It.
item.description: A Russian-speaking Aur0ra affiliate broke into seven companies by telling Cursor's AI agent the intrusions were authorised security testing, exposing the fact that no model provider can verify the one thing separating a penetration test from a crime.

item.title: The Labor Department Wants AI Companies to Tell It Which Jobs AI Is Taking
item.description: The Labor Department has signed data-sharing agreements with OpenAI, Google, Meta and Amazon to track AI's employment effects, filling a real measurement gap at a BLS that lost 20 percent of its staff, but handing the evidence supply to the firms with the biggest stake in the answer.

item.title: Ring Will Throw Away the Keys in 24 Hours. It Still Holds Them Long Enough to Run the AI.
item.description: Ring's TAKE encryption is a real privacy upgrade shipped on by default worldwide, but it is not end-to-end encryption: Ring still decrypts video inside an AWS Nitro Enclave and holds keys for up to 24 hours, a window users cannot audit.

item.title: OpenAI's Head of Data Centers Left in the Middle of the Largest Buildout in Company History
item.description: Chris Malone's exit after 17 months matters less as a single departure than as a window into how hard OpenAI's infrastructure job has become, with the role already split and leasing revived over building.

item.title: Meta Settles the Teen Harm Case for Up to $17 Billion — and Rewrites Instagram's Defaults
item.description: Meta ended a landmark state child-safety trial midway through week two by agreeing to pay up to $17 billion and accept court-ordered defaults on Instagram and Facebook for every U.S. user under 18, with a third of the money contingent on TikTok and YouTube signing similar terms.

item.title: SoftBank Is Shopping a $20 Billion Bond to Refinance Its OpenAI Bet
item.description: SoftBank is sounding out banks on a $10B-$20B dollar-and-euro bond, potentially September and possibly Asia's largest corporate deal of 2026, to refinance the $40 billion bridge loan underwriting its roughly $65 billion OpenAI stake.

item.title: Anthropic Will Tell Investors Its Market Is Worth $30 Trillion. Its Own Forecast Needs 0.65% of It.
item.description: Anthropic's record $30 trillion TAM is not a revenue forecast but a denominator, built by pricing human labor rather than software spending, and it exists to make the company's own $195 billion 2028 target look like a rounding error.

item.title: Amazon Is Shutting Mechanical Turk on September 30. The AI It Helped Train Took Its Job.
item.description: Amazon is closing Mechanical Turk on September 30 after 21 years, retiring the crowdsourcing marketplace that supplied the labeled data behind ImageNet and modern AI, as models now do the cheap classification work.

item.title: Moonshot Wants 30% of the Revenue. Microsoft, Amazon and Google Are Listening.
item.description: Moonshot AI is asking Microsoft, Amazon and Google for up to 30% of all Kimi K3 revenue on their clouds, testing whether commercial demand for a top-tier Chinese open-weight model outweighs the risk of partnering with a company Washington may blacklist.

item.title: Tencent-Backed Enflame Opens Books on a $892 Million Shanghai IPO
item.description: Enflame's $892 million STAR Market listing is the sharpest test yet of whether China's AI chip rally rests on fundamentals or on Nvidia's forced exit, given a 1.2 billion yuan loss and 83.8% revenue concentration in its own backer.

item.title: Mistral Sells Sovereignty Twice: A Hundreds-of-Millions Deal With Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN
item.description: Mistral has extended its European sovereign-AI pitch to Saudi Arabia in a hundreds-of-millions-euro framework with PIF-owned HUMAIN, trading Arabic frontier models and regulated-market access for Gulf compute capacity it cannot build fast enough at home.

item.title: IBM's Granite 4.2 Bets That Enterprises Want a 30B Agent Model They Can Own
item.description: IBM shipped Apache 2.0 reasoning models at 3B, 8B and 30B trained with agentic RL in live code, terminal and search environments, betting enterprise buyers will trade a capability gap against Qwen for weights they own outright.

item.title: Google Points Gemini Enterprise at Big Law — and at Harvey's Business Model
item.description: Google Cloud launched Gemini Enterprise for Legal in preview with Cleary Gottlieb, Freshfields, Weil and Williams & Connolly as design partners, connecting to Harvey, Legora, Thomson Reuters, iManage and Relativity while undercutting them on price.

item.title: Claude Now Carries One Memory Across Chat and Cowork. There Is No Way to Split It.
item.description: Anthropic merged Claude chat and Cowork into a single editable memory store on August 25, eliminating agent re-briefing but leaving users no way to separate work and personal context short of running two accounts.

item.title: Microsoft Will Put Saudi Arabia's Arabic Models Inside Foundry and Copilot
item.description: HUMAIN and Microsoft announced plans, not products: ALLAM is intended for Microsoft Foundry and eventually Microsoft 365 Copilot with no ship date, while the concrete piece is embedding HUMAIN engineers alongside Microsoft's Forward Deployed Engineers inside Saudi customer environments.

item.title: A German Broker Just Let ChatGPT and Claude Place Trades for a Million Customers
item.description: Scalable Capital has wired ChatGPT, Claude and Grok directly into a regulated European brokerage via MCP, giving over one million clients prompt-driven access to 60 billion euros in assets while keeping a human confirmation step on every trade.

item.title: OpenAI's Jalapeno Chip Claims 1.9x Blackwell's Work Per Watt, On OpenAI's Own Numbers
item.description: OpenAI's first custom inference ASIC posts 1.5x to 1.9x better throughput per kilowatt than Nvidia's Blackwell racks in benchmarks OpenAI ran itself, but the comparison excludes newer Nvidia hardware and rests on normalization choices that need scrutiny.

item.title: Samsung Put the Math Inside the Memory. It Claims an Eightfold Bandwidth Jump.
item.description: Samsung's LPDDR5X-PIM embeds MAC engines in all 16 DRAM banks to hit 614 GB/s internal bandwidth and triple LLM token throughput on edge silicon, but its fate hinges on JEDEC standardization and a named customer rather than the benchmarks.

item.title: An AI Read 500,000 DNA Sequences and Finally Pinned Down Biology's Fuzziest Gene Switch
item.description: UC San Diego researchers measured the activity of about 500,000 initiator variants and trained models that, for the first time, quantitatively predict where transcription starts, finding an active initiator in roughly 60% of focused human promoters.

item.title: Bill Gates Wants Some Jobs Legally Off-Limits to AI. He Floated 40 Percent.
item.description: Bill Gates is asking governments to legally reserve certain occupations for humans and tax AI tokens and robots, admitting he cannot get the protected share above 40 percent even in an extreme scenario.

item.title: London's Robotaxi Launch Slips. Waymo, Wayve and Baidu Are Waiting on a Document.
item.description: London's fully driverless robotaxi launch has slipped out of 2026 because Transport for London has not published the operator guidance companies need and the DVSA has approved zero vehicles under the new permit regime.

item.title: A Self-Hosted Git Server Bug Is Being Exploited. Federal Agencies Have Until Friday.
item.description: A CVSS 9.8 code injection flaw in self-hosted Gitea is under active exploitation and now carries a federal patch deadline, exposing the Git servers that increasingly feed and host AI coding agents.

item.title: Nvidia Told Its Biggest Customers AI Server Prices Are Going Up 15%. The Culprit Isnt the GPU.
item.description: Nvidia is raising AI server prices by more than 15% on Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems shipping from early 2027, driven not by GPU costs but by HBM and server DRAM now making up roughly a quarter of a high-end racks bill of materials.

item.title: Nvidias Groq 3 LPX Enters Full Production, Splitting Inference Into Two Different Chips
item.description: Nvidia moved Groq 3 LPX into full production, formalizing a split in AI inference where Rubin GPUs handle context prefill and dedicated LPX racks handle latency-sensitive token decode.

item.title: Nebius Asked the Bond Market for $4.5 Billion and Priced $5 Billion. No Board Seat Changed Hands.
item.description: Nebius $4.5B ask priced at $5.0B in convertible notes rather than venture equity, absorbing roughly 41% of the $11B raised across 60 AI rounds during Aug 17-23 and showing that AI infrastructure financing has migrated to the bond market.

item.title: Thomson Reuters Spent $40 Million to Build Its Own LLM. The Final Training Run Cost $450,000.
item.description: Thomson Reuters post-trained an open-weight base on Westlaw, Practical Law, Checkpoint and Reuters content for about $40M over two years, with a final training run near $450,000, showing vertical incumbents can own a domain model instead of renting frontier API tokens.

item.title: Toyota North America Says It Has 50 AI Agents in Production. Most Enterprises Still Have Zero.
item.description: Toyota Motor North Americas 50-plus production agents run on an in-house platform built on LangChain and LangGraph, and its edge is operational discipline rather than model access, which is exactly what the 89 percent of agent pilots that never reach production are missing.

item.title: DeepSeeks V4 Flash Can Finally See. For the First Time, There Are No Weights.
item.description: DeepSeek shipped its first image-capable V4 model on Aug 21 at $0.22 per million input tokens with no vision surcharge, but broke with precedent by releasing it API-only: no open weights, no license, no paper.

item.title: MCP Goes Stateless as Anthropic Takes Computer Use, Browser Use and the Skills API Out of Beta
item.description: The 2026-07-28 MCP spec deletes the session handshake, turning MCP servers into ordinary stateless HTTP workloads that scale behind a plain load balancer, and three weeks later Anthropic moved computer use, browser use, the Skills API and the Files API to general availability.

item.title: OpenAIs Ultrafast Mode Runs GPT-5.6 Sol 14x Faster. It Is the Cerebras Deal Wearing a Product Name.
item.description: Ultrafast is not a new model but the same GPT-5.6 Sol served on Cerebras wafer-scale silicon at up to 750 output tokens per second, sold as an invite-only API tier with no published price.

item.title: MiniMax Open-Sourced a Model That Writes a Five-Minute Song in One Pass
item.description: MiniMax released downloadable weights for a model that generates complete five-minute songs at 32 kHz stereo in a single pass on as little as 8 GB of VRAM, and published no training-data disclosure at all.

item.title: Harvey Built Its Flagship Legal Model on Kimi K3, and Its Whole Research Stack Runs on Chinese Open Weights
item.description: Harveys Tenet is a research preview post-trained from Moonshot AIs Kimi K3, and it is not isolated: Harveys diligence models are post-trained Zhipu GLM-5.2 and its firm-knowledge model is Alibaba Qwen3.8-27B, all served on American infrastructure.

item.title: NVIDIA Is Giving Away the Agent Trajectories Everyone Else Is Paying For
item.description: NVIDIA has published over 1.8 million agentic trajectories under CC BY 4.0 for commercial use, commoditizing the scarcest input in agent post-training, and distilling most of it from Chinese open-weight teacher models.

item.title: Google Clouds Answer to Rogue Agents: Give Every Agent an Identity and a Proxy
item.description: Google Cloud has made agent identity a first-class IAM principal with SPIFFE-based identities, an Agent Gateway behind Identity-Aware Proxy and inline Model Armor, but the two pieces the pitch leans on hardest, mandatory human approval and tamper-proof provenance, remain coming soon.

item.title: SpaceX and Nvidia Designed a Vera Rubin Rack for Orbit. The Heat Still Has to Get Out.
item.description: Nvidias August 24 announcement is mostly a terrestrial Vera CPU deal; the orbital Starmind satellite is a design commitment with a Q4 2027 launch window, and radiative-only heat rejection at 150 kW peak plus roughly 2x worse cost per watt remain unsolved in public.

item.title: Thailand Is Buying Premium AI Subscriptions for Five Million Citizens. The Screening Layer Is Doing the Heavy Lifting.
item.description: Thailands 1.62-billion-baht TH-AI Passport goes live on 31 August giving up to five million citizens a year of premium access to 30-plus foreign AI models, but the sovereignty case rests on an unaudited screening layer the platforms own privacy notice describes far more cautiously than ministers do.

item.title: The FTC Will Not Wait for an AI Law on Personalized Pricing. Its Proposal Turns on Disclosure, Not a Ban.
item.description: On August 19 the FTC voted 2-0 to propose an enforcement policy statement declaring that AI-set personalized prices are already reachable under Section 5 of the FTC Act, but the theory is disclosure rather than prohibition.

item.title: A Judge Doubts Metas Laid-Off Workers Can Block AI-Assisted Cuts. The Discovery Fight Is What Matters.
item.description: Judge Orrick signaled on Aug. 24 that 26 anonymous ex-Meta workers are unlikely to win a preliminary injunction over allegedly AI-assisted layoff selection, leaving the decisive question whether plaintiffs can ever compel disclosure of the scoring systems.

item.title: Hugging Face Explores a Sale at $13 Billion or More — Nearly Triple Its 2023 Valuation
item.description: Hugging Face has hired a bank to gauge buyer interest at $13 billion or more — nearly triple its 2023 valuation — but no bidder has been named and no deal reached.

item.title: Nvidia Is in Talks to Back Perplexity at More Than $30 Billion — a 50% Markup in a Year
item.description: Nvidia is reportedly negotiating an equity stake in Perplexity at over $30 billion — a 50%-plus markup in twelve months — on the strength of a $750 million revenue figure at least one outlet disputes.

item.title: XPeng's Robot Unit Raised $900 Million at $6.3 Billion — But Only $600 Million Came From Outside Investors
item.description: XPeng carved its robotics arm into a subsidiary called Dogotix at a $6.3 billion post-money valuation, but a third of the headline $900 million comes from XPeng itself and its own executives.

item.title: Amazon Raised Echo, Kindle and Fire TV Prices by Up to 60% — Squeezed by the Same AI Buildout It's Funding
item.description: Amazon abandoned its long-running loss-leader hardware strategy overnight, raising Echo, Kindle, Fire TV and eero prices by up to 60% because AI data centers have absorbed the memory supply its cheap devices depended on.

item.title: Quintessent Raises $40M Betting One Laser Can Replace Eight Inside AI Data Centers
item.description: Quintessent's $40M Series A funds a quantum-dot comb laser that emits eight DWDM wavelengths from a single chip, attacking both the indium phosphide shortage and the component-count fragility of optical links in AI clusters.

item.title: A Stealth Model Topped a Coding Benchmark on 10 Tasks. Then Someone Ran the Full Set.
item.description: Ox Alpha's viral 80% DeepSWE score came from a 10-task sample; the full run put it roughly level with GPT-5.6 Sol — after thousands of developers had already sent proprietary code to a lab nobody could name.

item.title: Alibaba Shipped Wan3.0 One Day After a $10.2 Billion Share Sale. Net Income Fell 76%.
item.description: Alibaba raised $10.2 billion in equity and shipped its longest video model in the same week its net income fell 76% on a 75% capex surge — trading current profit for position in generative video.

item.title: ChatGPT Ads Went Live in 31 European Markets. Free and Go Users Are the Product.
item.description: OpenAI turned on advertising for ChatGPT Free and Go users across 31 European markets, running contextual ads under GDPR 'legitimate interest' and personalized ads on opt-in consent — a consent-or-pay structure Irish regulators have not yet blessed.

item.title: Google's A2A Joins Anthropic's MCP Under One Roof. The Agent Protocol War Ended Before It Started.
item.description: Google's A2A now sits alongside Anthropic's MCP inside the Linux Foundation-directed Agentic AI Foundation — either genuine neutral standardization, or the eight companies with the most to gain quietly agreeing on the agent interoperability layer.

item.title: AWS Put a Price on Grounding: $7 per 1,000 Agent Web Searches
item.description: AWS's expansion of AgentCore Web Search to Ireland and Tokyo, plus per-call domain and date filters, turns retrieval into a metered utility at $7 per 1,000 queries — undercutting rival grounding APIs and squeezing independent search vendors.

item.title: Agent Memory Became a Benchmark Category in 2026 — Then the Benchmarks Started Failing Their Own Audits
item.description: Agent memory now has a real leaderboard with forty-point gaps between systems, but independent audits show the dominant benchmark has a scoring bug rendering roughly a quarter of it unscorable — so the gaps may measure the test more than the systems.

item.title: Multi-Agent Systems Are Wired Wrong. Two Papers Rewire Them at Runtime — A Third Asks If It Matters.
item.description: DyTopo and SYMPHONY show that rewiring agent communication at runtime beats fixed topologies by wide margins, but neither runs the one control — a single strong model at equal token budget — that a Stanford study says makes most multi-agent gains disappear.

item.title: Agent Skills Work — But Not for the Reason Everyone Assumed
item.description: A controlled study of 8,135 agent trial records finds SKILL.md-style artifacts help by stabilizing execution procedure, not by injecting missing knowledge — and that skill-retrieval precision collapses as libraries grow.

item.title: Three Weeks Into Real Enforcement, the EU AI Office Can Fine Frontier Labs. Its Evaluation Unit Has 36 People.
item.description: The EU AI Office gained real power on 2 August to compel documentation and fine providers up to €15M or 3% of global turnover, but with a 36-person evaluation unit and most member states yet to notify contact points, no formal case has been opened.

item.title: A Federal Judge Just Refused to Kill a ChatGPT Death Case — and the Product-Liability Theory With It
item.description: A federal refusal to stay Lyons v. OpenAI keeps a wrongful-death case alive alongside twelve coordinated California state suits, and the operative theory across all of them is product liability — not territory Section 230 has historically covered.
